newsitem.title: GERMANY: Crossair costs hit by Swissair route costs.
newsitem.headline: Crossair costs hit by Swissair route costs.

text.p: Crossair AG, the regional airline of the Swissair group, has suffered additional extra costs by taking over Swissair routes in 1995 and 1996, chief executive Moritz Suter said on Wednesday.
He was speaking at a news conference during the European Regional Airlines conference here.
Crossair was now concentrating on cost controls after sucessfully integrating some Swissair regional routes and charter flights of the group's subsidiary, Balair/CTA last year, he added.
Suter said pilot flying hours per year have fallen to 480 hours from 840 hours.
"We have a goal for next year of 700 hours per pilot. We want to get back to 800 hours by 1998," he said.
"To divide areas into European and long-haul is wrong. I would rather divide into low-revenue and high-revenue routes. In low-revenue areas, you have to put in low-cost capacity," he added.
Suter said that Switzerland has many unused traffic rights in Latin America, Asia and Australasia, which are not operated due to Swissair's high cost structures.
He declined to say whether Crossair would operate such routes or take over more Swissair routes, but said Crossair would always remain a niche carrier outside major markets.

Crossair will introduce two classes on selected jet routes from end-October, and would offer business passengers 25 percent more legroom than economy passengers. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
